title: Prompt Evaluation & Experimentation
description: Study build a fixed evaluation set, choose objective and rubric checks, run controlled prompt comparisons, and track regressions and version prompts. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Build a fixed evaluation set
lessons.description: Split development and held-out cases and record the evaluation version.
lessons.conceptOverview: Collect representative inputs, boundary cases and expected behavior before tuning. Keep a held-out set so prompt edits are not judged only on examples already used for iteration.
lessons.whyItMatters: Prompt tuning needs unseen evaluation cases.

lessons.title: Choose objective and rubric checks
lessons.description: Define separate completeness and presentation scores.
lessons.conceptOverview: Use exact parsing, field comparisons or executable checks where appropriate; use a clear human rubric for subjective qualities. Separate correctness, completeness and style instead of blending them into an opaque score.
lessons.whyItMatters: Evaluation should distinguish factual requirements from style.

lessons.title: Run controlled prompt comparisons
lessons.description: Design a comparison that isolates the example change.
lessons.conceptOverview: Compare prompt variants on the same cases and generation settings, with repeated runs when outputs vary. Change one factor at a time when trying to attribute the cause of an improvement.
lessons.whyItMatters: Controlled comparisons make prompt improvements interpretable.

lessons.title: Track regressions and version prompts
lessons.description: Add the convention to a regression gate and preserve the previous version.
lessons.conceptOverview: Version instructions, examples, schemas and evaluation results together. Inspect regressions by task category before replacing a prompt that already supports existing users.
lessons.whyItMatters: Prompt releases should preserve required existing behavior.
